set1.label: Alim Music
set1.note: Kenny Dixon Jr. takes the 1983 Brit jazz-funk holy grail and leaves the tape hiss in. Long, warm, unhurried — a Loft-logic opener that still moves.

set1.label: Defected
set1.note: 10:22 of Mr. K doing what the Edits catalogue always did — hold a disco groove at deep-house pace. Enormous amount of room to mix out of.

set1.label: R2 Records
set1.note: Karizma's Kaytronik alias rebuilding Crystal Waters. Two allowed-list names in one record and an instant crowd-recognition moment without playing the obvious version.

set1.label: Nervous Records
set1.note: Off the Grammy-nominated Expansions In The NYC. Claussell's Afro-Latin percussion under Vega's drums — the deepest possible way to raise the energy.

set1.label: Nervous Records
set1.note: Moodymann singing over a Vega rhythm section. Detroit and New York in one record — smiling, loose, unmistakably grown.

set1.label: Lovely Edits
set1.note: First volume of Parrish's Lovely Edits. Off-grid, hand-cut, and the drums hit far harder than the source. Awkward to mix, worth it.

set1.artist: Elements Of Life Featuring Josh Milan
set1.track: Let Us Shine (Josh Milan Honeycomb Remix)
set1.label: Vega Records
set1.note: Milan remixing a Vega band record with live keys and full gospel stack. This is the peak of the soulful phase — play it before the room is ready to think.

set1.label: Slip 'n' Slide
set1.note: The Josh Milan standard rebuilt for a modern floor. Keeps the vocal warmth but puts a much straighter kick under it — a clean hinge toward the deep section.

set1.label: Razor-N-Tape Reserve
set1.note: Carter doing the gear-change in a single record: disco source, house discipline, dub restraint. The bridge out of the opening hour.

set1.label: Masterjam
set1.note: Detroit sensibility, Chicago warmth, and a genuine Leroy Burgess vocal. The descent starts here — chords and space, no drop in energy.

set1.track: You Get Lost In It (Full Vocal Main Mix) (The Warehouse Project)
set1.label: Kaoz Theory
set1.note: From Spaces And Places, recorded club by club — this one at The Warehouse Project. RA called the album three hours of immaculate big-room house; reviewers keep naming this the best thing on it.

set1.label: Alleviated Records
set1.note: Title track of Larry Heard's first Mr. Fingers album in four years. The man who invented deep house, still doing jazz harmony on a drum machine.

set1.label: Alleviated Records
set1.note: Vault Sessions 2 — unreleased Heard material finally pressed. Introspective without being sleepy; the point in the set where the room gets quiet in a good way.

set1.track: Black Magic Woman (Joaquin's Edits & Overdubs Version)
set1.label: Sacred Medicine
set1.note: 14:40. Claussell overdubbing Ron Trent — two of the deepest catalogues in the document on one side of vinyl. Built for losing track of time; cut it early if the floor is impatient.

set1.label: Body 'N Deep
set1.note: Stripped, hypnotic Goldtone-lineage garage house. 8:24 of almost nothing changing — this is where the introspective turn starts to get pressure behind it.

set1.label: Mother Tongue / Neroli
set1.note: Chicago jazz-fusion chords over deep house drums, 2025 vintage. Keeps the funk in the room while the tempo creeps.

set1.label: Kaoz Theory
set1.note: The Sub Club cut from Spaces And Places — recorded for a room with a famously physical bottom end, and it shows. Bass weight arrives before the tempo does.

set1.label: Chicago Vinyl Records
set1.note: Hip house co-architect re-cutting his own 1988 acid record for now. 303 arrives, and it arrives cheerful rather than menacing — exactly the brief.

set1.label: TooDoo Records
set1.note: Drum-obsessed, rhythmically restless Baltimore funk. The funkiest possible route out of the deep section and into the pace.

set1.label: Phoenix G.
set1.note: All-hardware, raw jackin' house with enormous swing. Techno repetition, house soul — McBean's whole trick in one dub.

set1.label: Classic
set1.note: From Black Girl Magic. Mike Dunn on the mic, Warehouse lineage intact, and one of the hardest kicks she's put her name to.

set1.track: Bounce To The Beat (Chris Stussy Remix)
set1.label: Hard Times
set1.note: A 2024 remix package that put a Todd Terry record back on big floors. Blunt, loud, endlessly functional — the Terry brief, updated.

set1.label: Nervous Records
set1.note: Tribal, percussive, hypnotic — Tenaglia's Twilo grammar at 2023 volume. Seven minutes of pure body music.

set1.label: Classic
set1.note: From The Master's Plan on Classic. Gospel joy over a Detroit techno chassis — cheerful and hard at once, which is the whole ask.

set1.label: Classic
set1.note: Honey Dijon's spoken-word monologue over a Jersey-club-leaning kick. Widely picked out as the album's standout and it reads as both house and rave.

set1.label: fabric Originals
set1.note: Classically trained piano over K-Lone's sub weight. The clean handover point — still soulful, already garage.

set2.label: Swing City Records
set2.note: The first garage track ever to hit #1 on the Traxsource chart. Bumpy, bass-forward, built for the 4/4 half of the genre — the obvious opening salvo for the b2b.

set2.label: IFG Records
set2.note: The most rhythmically adventurous producer UKG ever produced, on a 4x4 refix with a ragga vocal. Instant hands-up without a hint of pop.

set2.label: IFG Records
set2.note: The VIP — harder drums, more sub. Hold it back as the answer to whatever she plays first.

set2.label: GD4YA
set2.note: From the South London vs North London split. Dark, sparse, sub-heavy 2-step from the man who led garage into dubstep — the tension move.

set2.label: GD4YA
set2.note: Title says the whole story: the road from garage to dubstep, mapped. Physical, spacious, and it makes anything played after it sound enormous.

set2.label: M-Plant
set2.note: M-Plant. Minimal Nation discipline with the Floorplan gospel lift — hard techno crowd bait that keeps the set's soul intact.

set2.label: Phoenix G.
set2.note: Hardware house pushed to techno pressure without losing the swing. Good landing pad if the b2b needs a breather that isn't a slow-down.

set2.label: Chicago Vinyl Records
set2.note: The Sneak remix is the harder half of the Acid Over 23 package — same 303, much more drum.

set2.label: Hardfloor
set2.note: Thirty-two years after Acperience 1, the layered-303 architecture returns. Reviewers rated the 2024 Hardfloor run their best in years.

set2.label: Hardfloor
set2.note: The B-side and the faster of the pair. If she's already at pace, skip 6 and go straight here.

set2.label: Ovum Recordings
set2.note: Built from a rediscovered tape of Wink's first LA rave set in 1994. Rolling groove, hypnotic acid, modern low end — the newest record in the document.

set2.label: Dexstar Recordings
set2.note: The Acid Queen of Djax-Up-Beats, still doing it in 2025. Title is the brief: rave, nation, 303.

set2.label: BPitch Control
set2.note: Emotional rave rather than functional techno — manipulated vocals, big drums, and it stays warm at speed. Ideal for a hard-techno room you don't want to lose to gloom.

set2.label: Rave The Planet
set2.note: The official 2025 Rave The Planet Parade anthem from the Love Parade's co-founder. Unashamedly euphoric — the closing statement if the b2b wants one.

bench.label: Classic
bench.note: Gospel house at full tilt — swap in for Summa Funk if the room wants vocals.

bench.label: Classic
bench.note: Dames Brown on vocals; the warmest cut on The Master's Plan.

bench.label: Mord
bench.note: Cisco Ferreira's hardware-first UK techno if the b2b goes harder than planned.

bench.label: City Road Records
bench.note: Bristol jungle veterans back on Independent Dealers — the break-4/4 escape hatch.

bench.label: Faithless
bench.note: Sister Bliss on a 2025 Faithless record. Rave-song energy; slightly too anthemic for the main table.

bench.label: Margeverse Limited
bench.note: Benched as the least underground option on the shortlist — held here in case the crowd wants a singalong.

bench.label: Rekids
bench.note: Raw Tones opener — rawer and more percussive than Igobolo if you want to start weirder.

bench.label: Classic
bench.note: Second Honey Dijon option for the funky pivot.

bench.label: Nervous Records
bench.note: Built on a Crystal Waters writing credit — two allowed-list names, but slower than Move That Body.

bench.label: Alleviated Records
bench.note: Vocal alternative to Andromeda One in the deep phase.

bench.label: Kaoz Theory
bench.note: The DC10 cut — harder and more direct than the other Spaces And Places picks.
